patterns.key_values: NSStatusItem fork-glyph + capsule open-highlight; dropdown ~240pt wide, 24pt row pitch, ~10pt corners, dark translucent material; 3 separator groups (state / config / app-commands); submenu chevrons one level; ellipsis grammar correct; Quit App + shortcut glyphs at foot
state-first ordering: disabled section header + live value at top ('Current Network -> Thunderbolt Ethernet'), config submenus, then app commands

signature_moves: Entire product surface is a single native NSMenu — zero custom window/toolbar/chrome; character is restraint (invisible-until-needed utility)
State-first menu IA: opens by answering 'what network am I on?' before offering any control (recognition over recall encoded in menu order)
One custom 'diverging fork / best-path' glyph carries all identity — glossy blue on the icon squircle, monochrome template in the menu bar; metaphor legible at both sizes
defects: none substantive — native menu grammar honoured throughout (ellipsis usage, 1-level submenus, <=3 groups, Title Case labels, dimmed-not-hidden shortcuts, system-rendered separators)

aesthetic.direction: invisible utility / template-default in the best sense — inherits the macOS menu aesthetic wholesale rather than committing a custom visual direction

psychology: Jakob's Law — leans on it entirely: exact system menu grammar means zero learning curve; users already know how to operate it
Recognition over recall — surfaces current network state at the top of the menu so the user never has to remember it
Hick's/Miller's Law — short menu (~8 items in 3 groups) keeps choice cost and working-memory load low
Aesthetic-Usability Effect — perceived quality comes from structural hygiene (correct native metrics) not decoration
Fitts's Law — full-width menu rows are large targets, though the menu-bar entry point itself is an inherently small top-right target
notes: Single asset is a MARKETING COMPOSITE (cover.jpg): device frame + gradient wallpaper + right-side brand headline 'Your Mac, always on the best network.' Only the menu-bar-extra + dropdown are design evidence. No raw @2x screenshot, no window/settings/empty-state surfaces. All menu metrics estimated at derived scale ~2.55px/pt; the 24pt row-pitch match to kit/macos-27.md is the main corroboration that these are real platform metrics. app icon.png (glossy blue fork glyph on white squircle, Liquid Glass) NOT digested here — Workflow A only; it corroborates the signature glyph. Second menu-bar toggle-glyph is unattributed (possibly a 2nd Mux indicator or unrelated extra). Corpus effect: first app profile, corpus stays Novice (1 app, 1 surface); no canon promotions possible from one app.
